messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: Posterior predictive simulations
parts:
Hi,

I am working on a problem of adaptive sample size. Assume we have acquired some data and estimated parameters. In my case data consists of L lots with S samples each and I am using a two-level hierarchical model for inter and intra lot variation (sigmaBetween and sigmaWithin). Then I generate predictive posterior for a Lnew lots S samples each using the technique analogous to replicated data in new schools (see BDA appendix C). The idea is for each draw from predictive posterior combine real data with simulated Lnew lots and perform the fit again to obtain posterior of sigmaBetweenNew for each draw. Then I combine all sigmaBetweenNew and get 95% credible interval. I increase Lnew until this credible interval dips below some threshold. This will tell me how many more lots I have to sample to obtain a good inter lot variability estimate. One problem is that I have to run MCMC multiple times (as many times as there are draws in sigmaBetween). Is there some more efficient way of doing this?

Thank for the insight,
Linas

The stan model for generating predictive posterior is attached.

messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: Re: Posterior predictive simulations
parts:
Hi,

I figured some workaround by running stan twice: using generated quantities to generate predictive posterior for new lot, then creating data sets in R (actual data+1 draw from predictive posterior), and then running stan second time (dissoLCmult) to estimate parameters for all data sets simultaneously. I have 1000 draws so estimating 1000 data sets takes serious time. Can anybody help to make the second model more efficient or suggest a better way how to determine additional # lots required to ensure that the estimate of inter lot variability is good enough.

Thank you,
Linas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Posterior predictive simulations
parts:
Move everything in the model down to generated quantities
and use the associated rngs.

You can probably speed things up a bit with vector operations,
but it's probably not worth it:

vector[N_SAMPLES_LOT] smp_pred[N_ADD_LOTS]

smp_pred[l, s] = normal_rng(0, 1);

...

smp_pred[l] = smp_pred[l] * sigmaWithin + processMean + sigmaBetween * i3;

It usually doesn't make much difference if it's not in
the context of autodiff (which generated quantities are not).

I'd think you could use the usual convergence measures. Run estimates
in multiple batches (say four batches of 50) and see if they've
converged, then try four batches of 100 and so on until you have enough.

- Bob
